tickets.title: F104 — focus-ring token plumbing (input/textarea/select adopt accent ring)
tickets.context: Lede is a React SPA (see /workspace/CLAUDE.md, /workspace/SPEC.md, /workspace/.ailoop/oracle.md — the frozen decisions live there and must NOT be re-litigated). BUG F104: form-field focus rings render Tailwind-default blue, not the accent. Root cause: `ui/input.tsx:13`, `ui/textarea.tsx:12`, `ui/select.tsx:18` use `focus-visible:ring-ring/25`, but `ring: "var(--accent)"` in `tailwind.config.ts` carries no `<alpha-value>` slot, so `ring-ring/25` can't resolve the alpha and falls back to rgba(59,130,246,.5) in BOTH themes. Buttons use plain `ring-ring` and are correct. FIX per oracle.md Locked (token-level fixes): make the ring alpha expressible — add an explicit `--ring-weak` token in tokens.css (or make `--accent` an RGB triple so `<alpha-value>` composes), wire tailwind.config.ts so `ring-ring/25` / a `ring-ring-weak` utility resolves to the accent at reduced alpha, and point the three inputs' focus-visible ring at it. Do NOT change the button ring language (it's correct) — converge the inputs onto the accent, don't diverge further. Visual identity is frozen: accent hue unchanged, only the plumbing.
tickets.acceptance:
- Add/extend a test (vitest or the design/e2e layer) that focuses an input, a textarea, and a select and asserts the computed focus ring resolves to the accent-derived value with alpha > 0 AND ring width > 0 in BOTH light and dark themes (a missing ring must FAIL — not merely 'not Tailwind blue', red-team #20).
- No off-palette rgba(59,130,246,...) remains on focused inputs in either theme.
- Baseline gate green (oracle.md).

tickets.title: F103 — docked panels open fully within viewport (CHROME-AGNOSTIC; re-gates in Phase 1)
tickets.context: See /workspace/SPEC.md F103. The three docked panels (`EntryEditor.tsx:212`, `ProfileEditor.tsx:205`, `LayoutEditor.tsx:95`) use `fixed right-6 top-6 z-20` while the header is `z-40`, so each panel opens half-buried: title + close button sliced, close hit-area partially blocked. FIX must be CHROME-AGNOSTIC (red-team #1): make the panel title AND close control fully within the viewport and hit-testable regardless of the header — do NOT hard-code around the current header's height/z, because Phase 1 (T020) DELETES the header and this exact assertion RE-RUNS unchanged as part of that gate. Solve via correct stacking + top offset that references the viewport/shell, not the soon-dead header. De-modal ban holds: these stay non-modal docked panels (no scrim, no aria-modal).
tickets.acceptance:
- e2e: with each docked panel open in turn, its title AND its close control are fully within the viewport and hit-testable via `elementFromPoint` (the point resolves to the panel's own element, not something overlapping it).
- NOT a stacking-order trick (red-team): the panel's title box must not intersect ANY other fixed/sticky chrome element in the DOM (measured generically, no header reference — pre-Phase-1 this catches overlapping the header; post-Phase-1 it's vacuously true, so the assertion survives). A diff that merely raises `z-20`→`z-50` while leaving `fixed right-6 top-6` untouched FAILS the gaming read — the fix must reposition relative to the shell, not out-race the header's z-index.
- No reference to a header element in the assertion (must survive the Phase 1 chrome merge and RE-RUN unchanged there).
- Baseline gate green.

tickets.title: F108 — login copy map, first-run microcopy via GET /api/auth/state (OQ8), hidden username
tickets.origin: spec F108 / OQ8 / Phase 0 — v4's ONE named backend exception
tickets.context: See /workspace/SPEC.md F108 + OQ8 + oracle.md Locked (login first-run). THREE parts: (1) BACKEND (the single sanctioned server change): add `GET /api/auth/state` → `{ setup: boolean }` in `src/server/routes/auth.ts` — public (the `/api/auth/` prefix is already in PUBLIC_PREFIXES per `src/server/auth.ts:7`), NO session required, returns ONLY the boolean, leaks no secrets. `setup === true` means a password IS configured (returning user); `setup === false` means first-run pending. Compute from `db.select().from(secrets).where(eq(secrets.id,1)).get()?.auth`. Existing endpoints for shape reference: setup/login/logout in the same file. (2) CLIENT: add a `getAuthState()` call in `src/client/api.ts` (mirror the existing auth helpers at lines 272-280); in `LoginGate.tsx`, render the 'First time here? This sets your password.' microcopy (currently unconditional at line 94) ONLY when `setup === false`; map raw error codes (`invalid_credentials`) to human copy (no `_`-code string on screen); add a hidden username field (`autocomplete="username"`) so password managers work. (3) TESTS: extend `test/api.auth.test.ts` for the new endpoint (answers without a session; returns only `{setup}`; reflects password-set state). This is the ONLY server change v4 permits — anything more is a scope tripwire.
tickets.acceptance:
- Server test: `GET /api/auth/state` returns 200 WITHOUT a session cookie; `Object.keys(body)` deep-equals `['setup']` EXACTLY (not merely 'no key material' — no `id`/`updatedAt`/extra fields); `setup` is false pre-setup and true after a password is set. RESTART-SAFE: after setup, re-instantiate the route/DB (or restart the test server) and confirm state still reports `true` — a module-level in-memory flag that doesn't survive restart FAILS (must read the `secrets` table).
- Unit-test the error-code→copy mapper as a PURE FUNCTION over ALL known server codes (`invalid_body`, `invalid_credentials`, `already_configured`): none returns raw/underscored text (mapping only the one live-clicked code and letting others fall through to `err.message` FAILS).
- e2e: wrong password ⇒ human copy (no `_`-code on screen); with `setup:false` the first-run hint renders, `setup:true` it does not (auth project fresh DB → false; applications reuses one → true); the e2e intercepts network and asserts a `GET /api/auth/state` call actually fires on login-page load AND no probing `POST /api/auth/setup` fires before the user submits.
- A hidden username input is present with computed `display !== none` (visually-hidden/clip technique, `tabindex="-1"`) — a `display:none` field that autofill ignores FAILS.
- Baseline gate green.
